Issues.Title: fix(zone.js): only cancel fake timers that fakeAsync scheduled
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md

- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #72070

A timer scheduled before `fakeAsync()` (for example the zoneless scheduler's `setTimeout`/`requestAnimationFrame` race armed by `TestBed.createComponent()`) can be cancelled inside `fakeAsync()` through the `ProxyZoneSpec`. `FakeAsyncTestZoneSpec.onCancelTask` then clears whichever fake timer has the same numeric id, so an unrelated fake timer silently disappears and `tick()` never runs it. The real timer is also never cleared natively.

## What is the new behavior?

`FakeAsyncTestZoneSpec` remembers which instance scheduled each macrotask. Cancelling a task it didn't schedule goes to the parent delegate, and a task scheduled by another fake zone is cleared from that zone's queue.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: Add WebMCP `outputSchema`
Issues.Body:
`outputSchema` was recently added to the spec and Chrome's WebMCP implementation: https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chrome-ai-dev-preview/c/aHZfIhWWzmM/m/NpIuxXxxBgAJ

This updates Angular's types to include `outputSchema` and hard-code a built in schema for signal forms tools.

Two things this PR does _not_ do at this time:
1. It does not validate that the result of `execute` actually matches the defined `outputSchema`. This likely requires a full JSON schema validator, which I don't want to get into just yet, especially while validation seems to be an open question in the spec right now. My hope is that this will either be built into browsers or at least documented as a much clearer concern for WebMCP tools. For now, I'm just taking the path of least resistance.
2. It does not type the return value of `execute` to match `outputSchema`. We currently rely on `webmcp-types` to do this for parameters and there is no support for that for `outputSchema` just yet.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add WebMCP `outputSchema`" (#72069)

Issues.Title: refactor(router): set route references on RouterState during activation
Issues.Body:
Split out from #72020 (first commit).

Remove `setRouterState` from the `RouterState` constructor and call it explicitly in `createEmptyState` and at the start of `ActivateRoutes.activate` instead of during `createRouterState`. Thread `parentRoute` through `setupAndRunResources` and `finalizeResources` so resource setup does not rely on `route.parent` before activation.

Because `createRouterState` runs before async work that can still cancel or redirect (and will move even earlier ahead of resolvers), setting `_routerState` there mutates reused `ActivatedRoute` instances prematurely and leaves their `firstChild` and `children` pointing at an uncommitted or abandoned tree if rollback occurs. Waiting until `ActivateRoutes.activate` keeps them on the current tree until activation, matching pre-1f287b9ba7 timing.

Related to b/584585009.

Issues.Title: refactor(core): quote InputMap constraint keys on directive declarations
Issues.Body:
`getInputsTypeExpression` in `@angular/compiler` emits `'alias'`, `'required'`, and `'isSignal'` as quoted string-literal property signatures in the `InputMap` type argument of `ɵɵDirectiveDeclaration` and `ɵɵComponentDeclaration` on `ɵdir` and `ɵcmp`. However, `ɵɵDirectiveDeclaration` and `ɵɵComponentDeclaration` in `@angular/core` declared those constraint keys as unquoted identifier property signatures (`{alias: string | null; required: boolean; isSignal?: boolean}`).

In standard TypeScript, quoted and unquoted property signatures are structurally identical. When a property-renaming safety pass rewrites unquoted identifier property signatures in `.d.ts` type literals while preserving quoted string-literal keys, the renamed constraint keys on `InputMap` no longer match the quoted `'alias'`, `'required'`, and `'isSignal'` keys emitted on preprocessed `ɵdir` and `ɵcmp` source declarations, failing `TS2344`.

This change quotes `'alias'`, `'required'`, and `'isSignal'` in the `InputMap` constraint on `ɵɵDirectiveDeclaration` and `ɵɵComponentDeclaration` so the declaration constraints match the quoted keys emitted by `@angular/compiler`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(core): quote InputMap constraint keys on directive declarations" (#72057)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): skip module_export_map walks when strategy ignores owning references
Issues.Body:
`propagate_owning_reference_validated` in `scope.rs` and `resolve_host_directive` in `component.rs` resolve a package entry point and walk its `module_export_map` so declarations and host directives from `.d.ts` files inherit the package's published specifier and export name. That mapping is only needed for strategies where `uses_owning_reference()` is `true` (`ApfImportStrategy`). Under `PrefixImportStrategy`, `uses_owning_reference()` is `false` and `emit` always derives module specifiers and export names directly from the declaring file (matching `ngtsc` omitting `AbsoluteModuleStrategy` from `ReferenceEmitter` when `_useHostForImportGeneration` is enabled).

Because workspace-prefixed and path-mapped module specifiers do not start with `.` or `/`, `.d.ts` `NgModule`s and directives imported under `PrefixImportStrategy` still recorded an `owning_reference` and walked barrel `.d.ts` re-export trees to compute owning references that `PrefixImportStrategy` ignores.

This change gates both `module_export_map` call sites on `uses_owning_reference()`, and also skips the export walk in `propagate_owning_reference_validated` when `owning_reference` is absent or all declarations already carry an `owning_reference`. In synthetic Bazel benchmark suites using `PrefixImportStrategy`, skipping unused export-map walks avoids 53% to 79% of initial `.d.ts` file parses, reduces persistent sidecar worker peak RSS by 20 to 52 MB, and cuts cold per-target analysis time on a warm worker by 66 to 134 ms.

Under `ApfImportStrategy`, `propagate_owning_reference_validated` still walks package export maps eagerly during scope construction rather than deferring to template-matched declarations, and falls back to a relative import instead of reporting `NG3004` when a declaration is missing from the barrel. Deferring that walk once template matching moves to Rust and reporting `NG3004` on template-matched declarations are tracked in a `TODO` on `propagate_owning_reference_validated` for follow-up changes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(compiler-cli): skip module_export_map walks when strategy ignores owning references" (#72055)

Issues.Title: fix(core): throw NG0512 instead of TypeError when hydration text node is missing
Issues.Body:
Given this template: ```html
{{ value }}
``` During hydration, Angular looks for the text node that the server rendered inside the ``. If the HTML from the server was changed and this text node is missing, dev mode throws a clear NG0500 error. But this check only runs in dev mode. Prior to this fix, production continued with the missing text node and failed on the first update of that binding with a raw error that doesn't say what went wrong: ``` TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'nodeValue') ``` With this fix, production throws NG0512 during hydration instead. Note that static text behaves differently. Nothing ever updates it, so it hydrated without an error before this fix and left a gap in the DOM. It now throws as well.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(core): throw NG0512 instead of TypeError when hydration text node is missing" (#72059)

Issues.Title: Reactive forms: transformedValue control shows an empty value after reset() followed by setting the previous value
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? forms ### Is this a regression? No ### Description A `FormValueControl` that uses `transformedValue` shows an empty input after a reactive form is reset and then set back to the value it had before the reset, in the same tick. ```ts import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, model } from '@angular/core'; import { FormControl, FormGroup, ReactiveFormsModule } from '@angular/forms'; import { FormValueControl, transformedValue } from '@angular/forms/signals'; import { bootstrapApplication } from '@angular/platform-browser'; @Component({ selector: 'app-text-input', changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, template: ``, }) export class TextInput implements FormValueControl { readonly value = model(null); protected readonly rawValue = transformedValue(this.value, { parse: (raw: string) => ({ value: raw || null }), format: (value: string | null) => value ?? '', }); } @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [ReactiveFormsModule, TextInput], changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, template: `

Control value: "{{ form.value.name }}"

`, }) export class App { protected readonly form = new FormGroup({ name: new FormControl('Ada') }); protected reload(): void { this.form.reset(); this.form.patchValue({ name: 'Ada' }); } } bootstrapApplication(App); ``` Click the button. The native input and the control value still show "Ada", but the custom input is empty. If change detection runs between `reset()` and `patchValue()`, everything stays in sync. #### Cause The reset propagation added in 849dba6 updates the raw value without updating the model or the cache of the last value written to the control: 1. On `FormResetEvent`, `NgControl` calls the reset callback with `control.value`, which is `null` here ([ng_control.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/1e6afa4cb84c/packages/forms/src/directives/ng_control.ts#L89-L103)). 2. `transformedValue` writes `format(null)` into its raw-value `linkedSignal` with `originalSet`, bypassing the model on purpose ([transformed_value.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/1e6afa4cb84c/packages/forms/signals/src/api/transformed_value.ts#L140-L144)). The control's `value` model is still `'Ada'`, because `NgControl` only writes it during change detection. 3. `patchValue({name: 'Ada'})` sets the `FormControl` back to `'Ada'`. 4. During change detection, `ngControlUpdate` skips the write because `customControlBindings.value` is still `'Ada'` ([ng_control.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/1e6afa4cb84c/packages/forms/src/directives/ng_control.ts#L381-L387)). The model never changes, so the `linkedSignal` never recomputes and keeps the empty raw value. The same commit handles this for CVA controls under `[formField]`: the `reset` binding in `control_cva.ts` writes the value and updates `bindings['controlValue']`, so later updates are compared against what the control really holds. The FVC path under `NgControl` has no equivalent. #### Proposed fix Mirror the CVA reset in `NgControl`. On `FormResetEvent`, before calling the reset callback, `NgControl` should write the reset value to the custom control's `value` model and update `customControlBindings.value` to match. Any pending custom value (for `updateOn: 'blur'` or `'submit'`) should be discarded at the same time, as `ngControlUpdate` already does when it overwrites the control. The model has to be written during the reset, not on the next change detection. If the write is deferred, `transformedValue` still formats the reset value while the model holds the old one, and when the previous value is written back the model doesn't change, so the raw value is never recomputed. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug The example in the description is a complete `src/main.ts`: paste it into a new Angular 22 project (for example `ng new --minimal`) and run `ng serve`. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw No errors ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.7 Angular : 22.2.6 Node.js : 22.23.3 Package Manager : yarn 1.22.22 Operating System : win32 x64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.7 │ 22.2.7 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.7 │ 22.2.7 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/forms │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ 7.8.2 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ ~6.0.3 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Anything else? #72065 looks related but is a different problem: there the control writes its own model under `[formField]`, and the remembered value in `control_custom.ts` is not updated. Here the control's model is never written; only the raw value of `transformedValue` is.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): support external modules, virtual IDs, and type-only import kinds in preprocessor
Issues.Body:
Bundler-backed AnalysisHost implementations resolve dependencies into both in-bundle modules and
bundle-external dependencies, distinguish runtime imports from type-only imports, and assign opaque
virtual module IDs that are not filesystem paths. Previously, the query engine assumed every
extracted specifier had uniform type-only semantics, treated resolved modules as in-project paths
unless they ended in .d.ts, and computed relative paths across emitted imports and debug metadata.

Classify extracted static imports, re-exports, dynamic import() expressions, and TSImportType
queries with exact ImportKind and type_only flags and forward both on ResolveRequest. Track
authoritative external module flags in FileIdInterner and QueryEngine so external modules pass
external = true to AnalysisHost::load, stay out of ProgramFiles, coordinator roots, and core
compilation, and preserve or rebase their original OwningReference specifiers instead of emitting
paths to resolved external files.

Propagate IdKind onto AnalysisResult, FileUpdate, FileInvalidation, and WASM ModuleRef entry
points. When either side of a reference or a compiled file carries IdKind::Virtual, emit the module
ID verbatim across cross-file import emission, class debug info, and HMR identifiers without path
diffing or rootDir stripping.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): support external modules, virtual IDs, and type-only import kinds in preprocessor" (#72066)

Issues.Title: fix(zone.js): add types condition to subpath exports
Issues.Body:
Please note that this fixes a **real** production issue; it wasn't found speculatively through AI code analysis.

Consider the following example:

```ts
if (ngDevMode) {
  await import('zone.js/plugins/task-tracking');
}
```

Under `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, `"node16"` or `"nodenext"` this fails to type-check:

```
Could not find a declaration file for module 'zone.js/plugins/task-tracking'.
'.../node_modules/zone.js/fesm2015/task-tracking.js' implicitly has an 'any' type.
```

The `exports` map declares `types` only on the root entry, so every subpath resolves to a bare `.js` file. Legacy `moduleResolution: "node"` ignores `exports` and finds files by path, which is why nobody hit this until the newer resolution modes became common.

Prior to this commit there was nothing a subpath `types` condition could point at, because the package shipped a single declaration file at its root. With this commit the build emits one declaration next to each bundle, and every subpath gets a `types` condition. The bundles patch globals and export nothing, so each declaration is `export {};` and adds no API surface to maintain.

Legacy `node` resolution does not change. Those subpaths did not resolve there before this commit either.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(zone.js): add types condition to subpath exports" (#72061)

Issues.Title: Signal Forms: Support optional one-way binding with [formField]
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

forms

### Description

Currently, [formField] always uses two-way binding, automatically updating the form model when the user changes a value.

It would be useful to support optional one-way binding, similar to model() or ngModel, where developers can choose between automatic synchronization and manually handling changes.

Example

With Angular Material's mat-select:
```html
<mat-select
  [formField]="form.userId"
  (selectionChange)="onUserChange($event.value)"
>
  ...
</mat-select>
```

When a user selects an option, [formField] automatically updates userId, while selectionChange also triggers a handler that updates the same field along with related properties:

```html
onUserChange(user: User) {
  this.formModel.update(form => ({
    ...form,
    userId: user.id,
    userName: user.name,
    userRole: user.role,
  }));
}
```

This creates two separate update paths for the same value

### Proposed solution

Allow developers to choose between automatic two-way binding and one-way binding with explicit change handling, similar to `model()` or `ngModel`.

It would also be useful to expose a change event, allowing developers to listen for user-initiated value changes.

For example (hypothetical API):

**Automatic two-way binding (default):**

```html
<mat-select [formField]="form.userId">
  ...
</mat-select>
```

**One-way binding with manual updates:**

```html
<mat-select
  [formField]="form.userId"
  [formFieldAutoUpdate]="false"
  (formFieldChange)="onUserChange($event)"
>
  ...
</mat-select>
```

**Two-way binding with change notifications:**

```html
<mat-select
  [formField]="form.userId"
  (formFieldChange)="onUserChange($event)"
>
  ...
</mat-select>
```

This would provide more flexibility while retaining the benefits of `[formField]`, such as validation, disabled state, and touched/dirty tracking, without requiring developers to use component-specific events or implement custom form controls.


### Alternatives considered

The current workaround is to avoid [formField] and use [value] with (selectionChange) to handle updates manually. However, this requires manually managing functionality that [formField] already provides, such as validation, disabled state, and touched/dirty tracking.

Another option is to keep [formField] and use (selectionChange) to update related fields, but this results in redundant updates to the same form value.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Signal Forms: Support optional one-way binding with [formField]" (#72058)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): trim preprocessor filesystem stats and memoize module resolution
Issues.Body:
During cold analysis and warm dependency invalidations, `ng-analyze` spent a substantial fraction of its I/O budget on redundant filesystem stats, path canonicalizations, and repeated module resolution probes:

- `OverlayFileSystem` called `canonicalize` on disallowed `.ts` and `.js` candidates even when they did not exist on disk or were non-symlinks whose basenames did not match any entry in `allowedSources`, walked all `rootDirs` prefixes instead of stopping at the longest matching prefix, statted missing `.ts` probes across `rootDirs` twice (`is_allowed` + `symlink_metadata`), blocked `.js`-named package directories (`zone.js`) when `allowedSources` was active, and cleared `is_allowed_cache` on physical file invalidations even when no virtual file existed.
- `load_and_resolve_tsconfig` eagerly statted every `.d.ts` entry in `files` even though `QueryEngine` loads declaration files lazily, and standalone invocations on Bazel `tsconfig.json` files without explicit `allowedSources` did not read `bazelOptions.compilationTargetSrc` / `bazelOpts.compilationTargetSrc` to bound `.ts` source probes and root discovery.
- `DefaultFsHost::resolve` ran `oxc_resolver` per importer file even for sibling importers in the same directory and re-canonicalized the same resolved dependency paths across directories.

This PR addresses these in three commits:
1. **`OverlayFileSystem` allowlist & `rootDirs` checks**: Encapsulates `SourceAllowlist` with `symlink_metadata` reuse and filename pre-filtering, allows directories, stops after the longest matching `rootDirs` prefix while preserving declaration priority on equal-length `rootDirs`, enforces `is_allowed` on `rootDirs` metadata fallbacks, fixes `preserve_symlinks` `cwd` existence checks, and keeps `is_allowed_cache` warm when `remove_virtual_file` removes nothing.
2. **`tsconfig` lazy `.d.ts` files & `compilationTargetSrc` fallback**: Skips eager `.d.ts` `fs.metadata` calls on `tsconfig.files` and folds `compilationTargetSrc` into `EffectiveConfig` once when `allowedSources` is unset.
3. **`DefaultFsHost` resolution & canonicalization memoization**: Memoizes per-directory `(importer_dir, specifier)` resolutions and canonicalized target paths in `DefaultFsHost` until `AnalysisHost::clear_cache()` runs.

### Observed Benchmark Outcomes

On Bazel compilation benchmarks (`subtask`, `plxcharts`, and multi-package suites):
- Cuts `ng-analyze` filesystem stats per target from ~14k–16k (`13,791`–`16,258` `fsStatCalls` on `subtask` prod, `2,533` in devmode) by eliminating eager `.d.ts` `tsconfig.files` stats, redundant `realpath` calls on non-existent or non-matching `.ts`/`.js` probes, and duplicate per-importer `oxc_resolver` + `canonicalize` passes.
- Combined with #72055 across the 8 PerfGate benchmark suites (retaining single-target warm worker reuse on same-variant edits while cold targets and `prod <-> devmode` variant switches initialize cleanly): keeps cold compile wall time within noise of baseline while cutting multi-target dependency rebuilds (`warm_cross_target`, which exercises cold target switching across a 3-target dependency chain) to 147–590 ms vs `ngtsc`'s 566–1,069 ms (25%–74% faster across all 8 suites).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): trim preprocessor filesystem stats and memoize module resolution" (#72056)

Issues.Title: Refactor(compiler-cli): avoid redundant JS fingerprinting in preprocessor
Issues.Body:
Reuse the bound fingerprint computed during `prepareChunk` when `processFile` runs for the same source content by carrying `boundFingerprints` on `ChunkContext`, avoiding duplicate `computeBoundFingerprint` calls on every TCB component file while keeping JS-side fingerprinting.

Also skip serializing `eagerlyUsedDeclarations` in `remoteScopeInputs` for declarations that are not remotely scoped, and only hash `declarationType` and `refInDeclaringModule` for remotely-scoped classes since `ɵɵsetComponentScope` reads no other fields.

Issues.Title: fix(router): navigate every time a RedirectCommand is thrown from an error boundary
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`triggerRedirectIfCommand` marks the thrown `RedirectCommand` with a symbol so the redirect is only dispatched once. The mark is never cleared, so if the same `RedirectCommand` instance is thrown again (for example a shared constant), the router no longer navigates and the user stays on the failing route.

Issue Number: #72027

## What is the new behavior?

The mark is removed, so every thrown `RedirectCommand` navigates. As discussed in the issue, the mark is not needed: a redirect is handled by the first outlet that catches it and is not propagated further, so it is not seen by several outlets.

The design doc and the angular.dev guide no longer describe the deduplication.

A test covers throwing the same `RedirectCommand` instance twice. The existing test for nested outlets (`dispatches RedirectCommand only once when bubbling through multiple boundaries`) is unchanged.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Testing note: I could not run Bazel on my machine (Windows). I verified the behavior against the published `22.3.0-rc.0` router with the mark removed, using the repro from the issue and the nested-outlet scenario (with and without `defaultErrorComponent`): the repro now navigates both times and the nested case still dispatches exactly once. The added spec itself has not been run locally, so please rely on CI.

Issues.Title: fix(common): normalize the exponent when rounding carries in exponential notation
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Numbers with more than 22 integer digits are formatted in exponential notation with a single integer digit in the mantissa. When rounding to the requested number of fraction digits carries into a new digit, `roundNumber` adds the carry to the mantissa instead of the exponent, so the result is not normalized:

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `formatNumber(9.99999e22, 'en')` | `10E+22` | `1E+23` |
| `formatNumber(9.99999e22, 'en', '1.2-2')` | `10.00E+22` | `1.00E+23` |
| `formatPercent(9.99999e22, 'en')` | `10E+24%` | `1E+25%` |
| `formatCurrency(9.99999e22, 'en', '$')` | `$10.00E+22` | `$1.00E+23` |

The same applies to `DecimalPipe`, `PercentPipe` and `CurrencyPipe`.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

In exponential notation the carry is folded into the exponent. All digits after the carry are zeros at that point, so the last one is dropped to keep the number of fraction digits unchanged. Numbers that are not in exponential notation are not affected.

The new spec fails without the change for every case that carries; the `'1.0-10'` case without a carry is included as a control.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

Issues.Title: ci: emit failure annotations using problem matchers and Bazel BEP
Issues.Body:
Alternative to #71938. Instead of wrapping `run:` commands, this uses GitHub Actions problem matchers plus a post step that reads the Bazel build event file, so the reason for a CI failure can be read from the check-run annotations API without downloading the job log.

- `.github/matchers/ci.json` has problem matchers for `tsc`, `tslint`, Bazel `ERROR:` lines, `ts-circular-deps` chains and `ng-dev` error lines.
- `scripts/ci/annotate-bazel-failures.mts` reads the build event file of the last Bazel invocation and prints one `::error` per failed target. Failed tests get the end of their test log, and build failures get the Bazel error followed by the compiler output. Flaky tests that passed on retry are skipped, nothing is printed if the last Bazel invocation succeeded, and anything past the 10 annotations GitHub keeps per step is summarized in the last one.
- `.github/actions/bazel-annotations` is a small local action that adds `--build_event_json_file` to `.bazelrc.user`, registers the matchers, and runs the script in a `post-if: failure()` step.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` registers the matchers and runs the script's unit tests in `lint`, and adds the action to the Bazel jobs. `pr.yml` is not changed.

Checked on a throwaway PR (#72047) that wires the same steps into `pr.yml` with intentional failures: a tslint error, a circular dependency, an invalid ngbot config, a `tsc` error, a failing Bazel test and a Bazel build failure.

Once the matching `angular/dev-infra` change (angular/dev-infra#4112) lands and is rolled in here, the local action, matcher file and script can be removed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "ci: emit failure annotations using problem matchers and Bazel BEP" (#72043)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): report the failing sequence sub-option in runner args errors
Issues.Body:
The `runnerArgs` validation reports every invalid value for the `--sequence` option with a single message that only lists the supported sub-option names: `--sequence.seed=-1` fails with 'The Vitest "--sequence" option requires only the following options: "--sequence.shuffle", "--sequence.seed".' although the user already used one of those options, and nothing states the actual value requirement.

Report each failing sub-option individually, matching the phrasing used for top-level options: an unknown name such as `--sequence.concurrent` is reported as not supported alongside the accepted names, and an invalid value such as `--sequence.seed=-1` is reported with the sub-option's own value requirement.

An invalid `--sequence.shuffle` value is not testable through the real Vitest parser, which types the option as a boolean flag and treats a provided value as a test file filter.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/pwa): support projects with the pre-v18 src/assets layout
Issues.Body:
`ng add @angular/pwa` decides between the `public` and legacy `src/assets` layouts with `host.exists(assetsDir)`, but `Tree.exists()` only matches files, so the legacy branch never runs and pre-v18 layout projects get the manifest and icons in a `public` directory their build does not serve. The manifest link injected into index.html then 404s and the application is not installable, while the schematic reports success.

Detect the directory through its entries instead and restore the layout that worked before the `public` directory support was introduced: the manifest is written to the source root, where the asset entry added to the workspace configuration and the injected manifest link already point, and the icons are written to the existing `assets` directory with the manifest referencing them as `assets/icons/*`. The workspace file is now written after the asset entry additions, which previously happened after `writeWorkspace()` and were never persisted. Projects using the `public` directory layout are unaffected.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/pwa): support projects with the pre-v18 src/assets layout" (#34734)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): handle done callbacks in focused and skipped tests
Issues.Body:
Similar to `transformPending`, `transformDoneCallback` previously only matched calls whose expression was the bare `it` identifier (or lifecycle hooks). Because `transformFocusedAndSkippedTests` runs earlier in the pipeline and rewrites `fit` to `it.only` and `xit` to `it.skip`, focused and skipped specs using a `done` callback were skipped by `transformDoneCallback`, leaving the `done` parameter and `done()`/`done.fail()` calls unmigrated.

Extract a shared `isItCallExpression` helper that matches `it`, `it.only`, and `it.skip`, and use it in both `transformPending` and `transformDoneCallback`.

Added unit tests covering `fit` and `xit` specs with `done` callbacks and verified with `pnpm bazel test //packages/schematics/angular:test`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@schematics/angular): handle done callbacks in focused and skipped tests" (#34732)

CoreSchemaRegistry was the only internal consumer of the deprecated PartiallyOrderedSet class. Issues.Title: feat(@angular/cli): forward arguments after -- to supporting builders
Issues.Body:
Allow architect-backed commands (`ng test`, `ng run`, etc.) to forward
arguments after `--` to builders that explicitly opt in via the
`"x-passthrough": true` schema keyword on an array option.

This adds a `passthrough` flag to `Option` parsed from `"x-passthrough"`
in `parseJsonSchemaToOptions`, enables `acceptsPassthroughArgs` on
`ArchitectBaseCommandModule`, and updates `runSingleTarget` to route
`passthroughArgs` to the target builder's `x-passthrough` option
(appending after any explicit option values) or throw a
`CommandModuleError` when the builder does not declare one.

The `@angular/build` `unit-test` builder marks `runnerArgs` with
`"x-passthrough": true` so `ng test -- <args>` forwards arguments to
Vitest. The `ng test` help description and Vitest snapshot e2e test are
updated accordingly.

Closes #32218
Closes #32726
Partially Addresses #32343

Issues.Title: feat(@angular/build): add runnerArgs option to unit-test builder
Issues.Body:
The unit-test builder now supports a `runnerArgs` option that provides
additional command line arguments to the Vitest runner. For example,
`ng test --runner-args=--update` updates existing snapshots and
`ng test --runner-args=--bail=1` stops the run after the first failure.
The option can also be configured within the `angular.json` file.

The arguments are parsed with the Vitest command line parser and then
validated against a list of supported Vitest options. The Vitest parser
accepts unknown options, command names, and test file filters without
error. The validation ensures that a misspelled or unsupported argument
fails the build with a descriptive message instead of being ignored.
Vitest options with an equivalent builder option, such as `--reporter`
and `--coverage`, are rejected with a reference to the builder option.

The initially supported Vitest options are `--allowOnly`, `--bail`,
`--disableConsoleIntercept`, `--expandSnapshotDiff`, `--maxWorkers`,
`--printConsoleTrace`, `--retry`, `--sequence.seed`,
`--sequence.shuffle`, `--shard`, `--testTimeout`, and `--update`.

The supported options take precedence over a Vitest configuration file
but not over the other builder options. The option is not available for
the Karma runner.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "feat(@angular/build): add runnerArgs option to unit-test builder" (#34717)

Issues.Title: dev-server keeps stale code of a linked (`file:`) library after `ng-packagr --watch` rebuilds it (rebuild reported, restart required)
Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

In a workspace with an application and a separate Angular library linked with a `file:` dependency, rebuilding the library in watch mode makes `ng serve` print "Application bundle generation complete", but the application bundle (`main.js`) still contains the **previous** compiled code of the library. The new code only appears after stopping and restarting `ng serve`.

The source map embedded in the same `main.js` already contains the **new** library source (`sourcesContent`), while the code is the old one. So the updated `.map` file seems to be re-read, but the content of `libreria.mjs` is reused from a previous build.

I could not determine whether this is the in-memory load cache, the file watcher, or something else.

### Minimal Reproduction

**Setup**

- Windows, project and library in sibling folders (`D:\...\proyecto-22` and `D:\...\libreria-22`).
- Library built with `ng build libreria --watch --configuration development` (ng-packagr).
- App `package.json`: `"libreria": "file:../libreria-22/dist/libreria"` (npm `install-links=false`, so `node_modules/libreria` is a Junction to `libreria-22\dist\libreria`).
- `preserveSymlinks` is not set (enabling it is not an option for me: the library sources then resolve under the app's folder and breakpoints in the library do not bind in VS Code).
- `angular.json` of the app:

  ```json
  "build": {
    "configurations": {
      "development": {
        "optimization": false,
        "extractLicenses": false,
        "sourceMap": { "scripts": true, "styles": true, "vendor": true }
      }
    }
  },
  "serve": {
    "options": {
      "poll": 1000,
      "prebundle": { "exclude": ["libreria"] }
    }
  }
  ```

- Angular CLI cache enabled (default).

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create the app and a library (`ng new`, `ng generate library libreria`), and build the library once into `dist/libreria`.
2. In the app, add `"libreria": "file:../libreria-22/dist/libreria"` and run `npm install`.
3. In the library, create a service with a method containing `console.log('v1')`, and call it from the app's root component.
4. Run `ng build libreria --watch --configuration development` in the library, and `ng serve` in the app.
5. Change the log in the library service to `console.log('v2')` and wait until ng-packagr finishes.

**Expected:** the dev-server rebuilds and the app runs `v2`.

**Actual:** the terminal prints "Application bundle generation complete" but the app still runs `v1`. Searching `main.js` shows the old code:

```js
// ../libreria-22/dist/libreria/fesm2022/libreria.mjs
...
console.log("v1");   // old code
```

while the embedded source map has the new source:

```
sourcesContent: "... console.log('v2'); ..."
```

`dist/libreria/fesm2022/libreria.mjs` on disk does contain the new code. Stopping and restarting `ng serve` fixes it.

**Things I tried without success**

- `poll: 1000` in `serve.options` (with restart).
- Deleting `.angular/cache` and restarting (works until the next library change).
- `prebundle.exclude` with the package name.
- Starting from a shell with the drive letter in uppercase (`D:`) instead of lowercase. <remove this line if you did not launch `ng serve` from that shell>

### Minimum Reproduction

https://github.com/LuisEscamillaMartin/repro-linked-lib-stale

### Exception or Error

```text
No error. The build reports success.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : win32 x64
```

### Anything else relevant?

Without `preserveSymlinks`, the library is bundled into `main.js` from its real path (`../libreria-22/dist/libreria/fesm2022/libreria.mjs`), outside `node_modules`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "dev-server keeps stale code of a linked (`file:`) library after `ng-packagr --watch` rebuilds it (rebuild reported, restart required)" (#34728)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): rebase Vitest incremental paths when workspace root is aliased
Issues.Body:
When `vitestConfig.root` differs from `workspaceRoot` (such as with symlinks or Windows `subst` drives), `VitestExecutor` still invalidated and queried test specifications during incremental watch-mode rebuilds using the un-rebased `workspaceRoot` paths. Because Vitest keys its module graph and test specifications against `vitest.config.root`, incremental re-runs could fail to invalidate cached modules or locate the affected test specifications.

To address this, extract a `rebasePath` helper in `plugins.ts` that converts paths between roots while leaving paths that cannot be expressed relative to the original root (such as files on a different Windows drive) unchanged instead of concatenating them. `VitestExecutor` now uses this helper during incremental rebuilds to rebase modified output and source file paths onto `vitest.config.root` when the root is aliased. Additionally, `configureVitest` now rebases from the original plugin options rather than mutating from the previous root so repeated invocations remain idempotent. `plugins_spec.ts` is expanded to cover `rebasePath`, `angular:` virtual entries, absolute setup files under coverage, and repeated `configureVitest` calls, and a new `executor_spec.ts` covers the incremental rebuild paths.

Issues.Title: Font inlining cache is not created or reused
Issues.Body:
Hi! I found two issues with the font stylesheet disk cache: the cache directory isn't created automatically, and even when it exists, valid cached CSS is deleted instead of reused.

### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

I haven't verified the last working version.

### Description

When font inlining is enabled, the CLI can cache stylesheets fetched from Google Fonts. However, the cache currently does not prevent repeated downloads. A build can fail when the font request is unavailable, even after the same stylesheet was successfully cached by the previous build.

### Minimal Reproduction

[Minimal reproduction and run instructions](https://github.com/nagahara-naoki/angular-cli/tree/repro-font-inline-cache)

The application uses Angular CLI and `@angular/build` 22.2.6, with persistent caching and font inlining enabled. Its global stylesheet imports:

```css
@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto:wght@400&display=swap");
```

Run locally to test the disk cache across separate CLI builds. The following commands are for macOS/Linux.

**1. Build with an internet connection.**

```sh
git clone --single-branch --branch repro-font-inline-cache https://github.com/nagahara-naoki/angular-cli.git font-cache-repro
cd font-cache-repro
npm ci
npm run build
ls .angular/cache/22.2.6/repro/angular-build-fonts
```

The build succeeds, but the font cache directory does not exist.

**2. Create the missing directory and build again while online.**

```sh
mkdir -p .angular/cache/22.2.6/repro/angular-build-fonts
npm run build
ls .angular/cache/22.2.6/repro/angular-build-fonts
```

The build succeeds and creates one cache file.

**3. Build again with an unreachable HTTPS proxy.**

```sh
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 npm run build
ls .angular/cache/22.2.6/repro/angular-build-fonts
```

The proxy setting applies only to that command, allowing the font request to fail without changing system network settings.

The build fails, and the previously saved cache file has been deleted. The directory is now empty.

### Expected Behavior

The CLI creates the cache directory automatically. Once the font stylesheet is cached, subsequent builds reuse it without requesting the same URL again.

### Actual Behavior

The directory is not created automatically. After creating it manually, the next build discards valid cached content and attempts another download. If that request fails, the build fails too.

### Exception or Error

```text
Failed to inline external stylesheet 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto:wght@400&display=swap'.

Error: Inlining of fonts failed. An error has occurred while retrieving https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto:wght@400&display=swap over the internet.
connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.6
Angular: 22.2.6
@angular/build: 22.2.6
Node.js: 24.22.2
npm: 11.19.1
TypeScript: 6.0.3
OS: macOS 26.5.2, arm64
```

### Anything else relevant?

The same causes are present in `InlineFontsProcessor` at repository commit `8b26efa1ba2b922d459f88add85e7e9a9a1dd9de`:

- [Cache reads](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/8b26efa1ba2b922d459f88add85e7e9a9a1dd9de/packages/angular/build/src/utils/index-file/inline-fonts.ts#L184) compute a Base64 SHA-256 hash, while [cache writes](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/8b26efa1ba2b922d459f88add85e7e9a9a1dd9de/packages/angular/build/src/utils/index-file/inline-fonts.ts#L258) store a hexadecimal hash. These cannot match, so valid cache files are treated as corrupted and removed.
- The write path calls `writeFile` without creating the parent directory. The resulting error is caught, so the build succeeds without saving the stylesheet.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): restore font stylesheet caching
Issues.Body:
Hi! This fixes the font stylesheet disk cache so builds can save downloaded CSS and reuse it on later runs.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

## What is the current behavior?

The font cache directory is not created automatically, so saving the stylesheet fails silently. Even when the directory exists, cache reads compare a Base64 hash against the hexadecimal hash stored by cache writes. Valid cache files are consequently deleted and downloaded again.

Fixes #34719.

## What is the new behavior?

- Create the parent directory recursively before writing a cached stylesheet.
- Validate cached content using the existing hexadecimal hash format, allowing subsequent processors to reuse the file without another request.

Add regression coverage for directory creation, reuse across processor instances, corrupted cache entries, disabled caching, and cache write failures.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

This fixes the existing font stylesheet cache path. No documentation update is needed for this internal correction.

The reproduction in #34719 was verified with actual CLI 22.2.6 builds: the initial build did not create the cache directory; after creating it manually, the next build discarded the saved file and failed when the font request was unavailable.

Validation: repository formatting, targeted ESLint, and `git diff --check`. The added regression tests have not been executed locally.

Issues.Title: Angular SSR prerender chunk-name collision desynchronizes Content-Length and contaminates other users' responses behind a proxy
Issues.Body:
### Command build ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description This is another piece of the prerender path from #34474 and #34569, which I reported. #34493 escaped the manifest key and the `import()` specifier, and #34570 validates the parameter values, but the chunk's file name still goes through its own `replace`, and two different pages can end up with the same one: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/72f44d79cb577821bbfa849f5bb3b41eee87c2ab/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/manifest.ts#L173 So `legal/privacy/index.html` and `legal_privacy/index.html` get the same file, and the later one replaces the earlier: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/72f44d79cb577821bbfa849f5bb3b41eee87c2ab/packages/angular/build/src/builders/application/execute-post-bundle.ts#L221-L228 The manifest still has both pages, each with its own `size` and `hash`, and the server sends those with whatever the shared file holds: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/72f44d79cb577821bbfa849f5bb3b41eee87c2ab/packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts#L233-L246 N pages in the manifest, N - 1 files in `dist`, and `ng build` exits 0 with no warning. Those paths come from `getPrerenderParams()`, which is application data: the docs read it from a service, and [GHSA-w34w-96hf-98hj](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/security/advisories/GHSA-w34w-96hf-98hj) says it "commonly fetches dynamic identifiers or slugs from an external API, CMS, or database". Anyone who can create one record can take the chunk of a page that already exists. The app in the repro uses the workaround from that advisory as it is, allowlist `/^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]+$/` included, and its store also caps the length, reserves names and rejects duplicates ignoring case. These records still pass, and so does the #34570 validator, because `legal_privacy` and `legal/privacy` only become equal inside that `replace`: | Records created through the app's API | Page that is lost | Result | | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | | account `legal_privacy` | the site's `/legal/privacy` | the URL serves the attacker's profile | | account `acme`, project `docs_intro` | `/acme_docs/intro`, another account's project | the URL serves `acme/docs_intro` | | `mallory_dev/tools` and `mallory/dev_tools` | `/mallory/dev_tools` | behind nginx with a cache, one request puts their script on every URL | It only needs routes that can make a pair: two parameters (`:user/:project`), a root `:user` next to a static page two segments deep, or two parameter routes of different depth under one prefix, like the SSR guide's own `post/:id` and `post/:id/**`, where the id `1_foo_3` takes the chunk of `post/1/foo/3`. Names that differ only in `.`, `_` and `/` aren't rare either: npm has [rejected them since 2017](https://blog.npmjs.org/post/168978377570/new-package-moniker-rules) and PyPI [normalizes](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/) them, and among the 4,681,490 public npm names 697 groups would still lose a page under `:name` and `:scope/:name`. **1. The lost page.** `/legal/privacy` answers 200 with the attacker's profile, under the length and the `ETag` of the page that's gone: ```text $ curl -s -D- http://localhost:4000/legal/privacy stalls 6.06 s, then curl: (18) content-length: 2647 etag: "85d6085a71e5686e" Profile of legal_privacy

legal_privacy

Our privacy policy has moved.

Website ``` The body is 1,375 bytes, so the document never finishes loading. Chrome 156 keeps the profile on screen and Angular never boots to replace it. `If-None-Match` with that `ETag` gets a 304, and it still does after the record is deleted and the site rebuilt: a Chrome profile that visited during the collision kept the attacker's page on the fixed build until a forced reload. On `/acme_docs/intro` a browser shows the right project once Angular boots, but crawlers and link previews keep the other account's. **2. Which of the two survives.** The build machine decides, not the content. Prerendering uses `max(availableParallelism() - 1, 1)` workers, so on 2 CPUs there's one worker and nothing races: 10 of 10 builds lost the pages that existed first, and 2 CPUs is the default on hosted CI runners. In a bigger lab the record's page stayed in 56 of 56 builds on 2 CPUs, and 32 of 32 on 4 and 8 for sites of 70 and 610 routes. All 265 exited 0 with no warning. Only a small site on many CPUs races. **3. On Windows, case alone is enough.** NTFS is case-insensitive, so two chunk names that differ only in case are one file, and the last write wins. The build never notices: the two paths differ as strings, so the duplicate check above doesn't fire, the manifest keeps both entries pointing at what it thinks are two files, and `tools/check-dist.mjs` sees nothing either. No store and no `_` involved, just two routes: ```ts { path: 'archive', component: Archive, title: 'Archive' }, { path: 'Archive', component: CapitalArchive, title: 'Capital Archive' }, ``` ```text Prerendered 14 static routes. exit 0, no warning $ node tools/check-dist.mjs 16 pages, 16 chunks, 0 shared it reports no collision server/assets-chunks/ archive_index_html.mjs one file where the manifest names two browser/ archive/index.html one directory, holding the capital page GET /Archive 200 declared 1000 sent 1000 Capital Archive GET /archive 200 declared 955 sent 1000 Capital Archive <-- not the declared length ``` `/archive` serves the other route's page under its own length and `ETag`, 45 bytes over what it declared. The copy under `dist/browser` collapsed the same way, so here a static host is affected too. Measured on Windows 11, NTFS, `@angular/build` 22.2.7, Node 24.16.0. **4. Behind a proxy it reaches other users.** The server writes more bytes than it declared, because the length comes from the lost page and the bytes from the surviving one. A proxy with upstream keep-alive stops at `Content-Length`, calls the response done, and leaves the rest on the pooled connection, where it answers whichever request gets that connection next. Those bytes are the attacker's record, so the attacker writes them: a complete `text/javascript` response in one project description, with the other sized so the declared length ends where it begins. Both go in as plain text. With `proxy_cache` in front it is stored under the URL that next request asked for. One request per URL took all five URLs of the lab site, the main bundle included, and from then on the cache served it with no attacker traffic at all: ```text $ lab tools/traffic.mjs 8 0 10 8 visitors, nobody attacking visitor requests 47335 got what they asked for 0 got the attacker's script 47335 (100.0 %) answered from the cache 47335 attacker requests 0 ``` A second run took 4 of the 5 URLs, 80.0 %. A request that doesn't land stores the real page instead, so it's one try per URL per `proxy_cache_valid` period, and right after a deployment the cache holds none of those URLs yet. Two things bound it. The link needs a round trip, because the leftover bytes have to arrive after the proxy has handed the connection over and not while it's idle in the pool: 0 % with netem removed (two containers on one host), 73.3 % at 300 µs, 100 % at 1 ms and above. And the declared length has to land at the end of the server's first write burst: one value in the range I swept worked and the rest landed 0 %. Each pair gets its own chunk, though, so one build can hold several pairs at several lengths. Issues.Title: Template diagnostics not updated in watch mode on Windows when the type-check block is unchanged
Issues.Body:
### Command serve ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description On Windows, during `ng serve`, a template edit that changes Angular diagnostics without changing the generated type-check code is not diagnosed: a stray `` (`NG5002`) still ends with "Application bundle generation complete", and `[attr.width.px]` never shows `NG8106`. Linux and `ng build` report both correctly. The resource check that invalidates `diagnosticCache` ([aot-compilation.ts#L334](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/8b26efa1ba2b922d459f88add85e7e9a9a1dd9de/packages/angular/build/src/tools/angular/compilation/aot-compilation.ts#L334)) looks up forward-slash paths from `getResourceDependencies()` in `modifiedFiles`, which holds `path.normalize`d backslash paths ([source-file-cache.ts#L42](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/8b26efa1ba2b922d459f88add85e7e9a9a1dd9de/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/angular/source-file-cache.ts#L42)), so it never matches on Windows: ``` modifiedFiles: ["C:\\repro\\src\\app\\app.html"] resourceDependencies: ["C:/repro/src/app/app.html"] match: false (Linux: true) ``` Edits that change the `.ngtypecheck.ts` shim are still picked up by the TypeScript builder; the others rely on this check alone. A possible fix is `hostOptions.modifiedFiles.has(path.normalize(resourceDependency))`. ### Minimal Reproduction Repro: https://github.com/te-gis-dev/ng-stale-template-diagnostics (`node repro.mjs` runs all steps against `ng serve` and restores the files). With `@angular/build` 22.2.7, run `ng serve`, then: 1. Append `` to `src/app/app.html`. Expected `NG5002`; actual on Windows: build completes, no error. 2. Revert, then append `

`. Expected `NG8106` warning; actual on Windows: none. 3. Add a blank line to `src/app/app.ts`. The missing diagnostics appear. | Setup | Stray `` | `[attr.width.px]` | | --- | --- | --- | | 22.2.7, Windows 11, Node 26.12.1 | not reported | not reported | | 22.2.7, Linux (Docker `node:24`) | correct | correct | ### Exception or Error ```text Windows: Application bundle generation complete. Linux: ✘ [ERROR] NG5002: Unexpected closing tag "span". It may happen when the tag has already been closed by another tag. For more info see https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/syntax.html#closing-elements-that-have-implied-end-tags [plugin angular-compiler] Application bundle generation failed. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.7 Angular : 22.2.6 Node.js : 26.12.1 Package Manager : npm 11.16.0 Operating System : win32 x64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.7 │ 22.2.7 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.7 │ 22.2.7 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/forms │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/router │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ ~7.8.0 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ 6.0.3 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Anything else relevant? - Windows only; drive-letter casing is not involved. - Latent on `main` / 22.3.0-rc.0: #34173 marks the component affected through Angular's incremental compilation first, but the lookup is still `false` on Windows. The check has never matched there since #25940. - On 22.2.x it also locks in the stale cached error fixed by #34173: while it is served, every template edit on Windows is ignored (`repro.mjs` steps 1-6).

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): keep generated locale polyfills cacheable
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the project guidelines.
- [x] Extended the existing i18n E2E test.

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

In a localized AOT build without additional polyfills, the CLI-generated polyfills bundle only sets the locale and loads Angular locale data. Editing an application translation still changes its URL because esbuild includes the translation-file digest in the filename hash.

Part of #30675; follows the feedback on #34673.

## What is the new behavior?

Use the selected locales and their Angular locale data as the hash input for this generated bundle before esbuild assigns the filename. There is still one shared filename across locales, and no output files or imports are rewritten for hashing. Application chunks, workers, user-supplied polyfills, and watch builds retain their current hashing.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

Issues.Body:
Extends the Vitest snapshot e2e test to cover updating existing snapshots after a mismatch. Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): resolve Vitest artifacts when workspace root is aliased
Issues.Body:
Starting in Vite 8.3.8 (`vitejs/vite@b643046`), `windowsLazyRealpathSync` calls `fs.realpathSync.native` synchronously on `config.root`, which resolves Windows `subst` drives and symlinks to their underlying physical path (e.g., `D:/.../test-project`) while the Angular CLI's `workspaceRoot` retains the logical path (`X:\test-project`).

This caused three issues during Vitest execution on aliased roots:
1. Vitest resolves relative `setupFiles` and test files against `vitestConfig.root`, which did not match `workspaceRoot` or the `testFileToEntryPoint` map in `angular:test-in-memory-provider`.
2. Passing absolute `workspaceRoot` paths in `test.include` caused `tinyglobby` (running with `cwd: vitestConfig.root`) to produce cross-drive relative paths (`../../../../X:/...`) that resolved to invalid paths (`D:/X:/...`).
3. Resolving virtual setup files under `vitestConfig.root` while resolving on-disk spec files under `workspaceRoot` caused bare package imports (such as `@angular/core/testing`) to be loaded twice from both drives.

To fix this:
- Pass workspace-relative paths in `test.include` in `VitestExecutor`.
- Rebase `workspaceRoot`, `testFileToEntryPoint`, and `setupFileSet` in `createVitestPlugins` (`configureVitest`) when `vitestConfig.root` differs from `workspaceRoot`.

Issues.Title: fix(material/dialog): prevent visual jump by removing open class together with closing class
Issues.Body:
When `_startExitAnimation()` is called, `mdc-dialog--open` was previously removed synchronously while `mdc-dialog--closing` was scheduled in a `requestAnimationFrame` callback.

When `close()` is called from within a `requestAnimationFrame` callback (such as during zoneless change detection scheduling or reactive effect updates), the nested rAF is deferred to the next frame. During that intermediate frame, the dialog container renders with neither class, applying the base un-opened styles (`scale(0.8)` / `opacity: 0`) and causing the dialog surface to visibly shrink and then snap back when `mdc-dialog--closing` is applied.

### Solution

Remove `mdc-dialog--open` and add `mdc-dialog--closing` together within the `requestAnimationFrame` callback so the container transitions directly from the open state to the closing state without an intermediate class-less frame. When animations are disabled, `mdc-dialog--open` is removed immediately in the non-animated branch.

### Verification

- Ran Prettier format check: passed (clean formatting).
- TypeScript compile / typecheck (`tsc -p src/material/tsconfig.json --noEmit`): clean on dialog files (0 errors).
- Added unit test in `src/material/dialog/dialog.spec.ts` asserting that `mdc-dialog--open` is not removed prematurely before the closing animation frame executes.

Fixes #34123

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/text-field): defer autosize checks until view initialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`CdkTextareaAutosize` can cache the textarea line height during its first `ngDoCheck`, before dynamic host classes have been applied. With `matInput` inside `mat-form-field`, this means measuring the browser default font instead of the inherited font. The resulting minimum and maximum heights remain incorrect until a window resize clears the cache.

Skip automatic checks until the view has initialized, allowing the existing `ngAfterViewInit` resize to perform the initial measurement after host bindings have been applied.

For example, a textarea with a 50px line height and limits of 2–5 rows now starts with `min-height: 100px` and `max-height: 250px`.

Fixes #33944.

## Testing

Added regression tests for both a CDK textarea with a dynamic host class and a `matInput` textarea inside `mat-form-field`.

- Without the fix: both new tests fail; the existing 130 tests pass.
- With the fix: all 132 tests pass in Chromium (28 CDK text-field and 104 Material input tests).
- Existing coverage includes initial content and placeholder sizing, row limits, programmatic value changes, window resizing, and disabling/re-enabling autosize.
- Repository formatting applied to all changed files.

```sh
pnpm bazel test //src/cdk/text-field:unit_tests_chromium //src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium --test_output=errors
```

Issues.Title: bug(material/core): dark on-surface-variant uses neutral-variant 90 instead of 80
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

18.1.x

### Description

In the dark scheme, `on-surface-variant` maps to `neutral-variant` tone 90 ([`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24)). The Material color spec maps it to tone 80:

- [material-color-utilities `color_spec_2021.ts`](https://github.com/material-foundation/material-color-utilities/blob/main/typescript/dynamiccolor/color_spec_2021.ts): `onSurfaceVariant` → `tone: (s) => s.isDark ? 80 : 30`, unchanged since 2023.
- [material-web tokens v0_192](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/v0_192/_md-sys-color.scss): `neutral-variant80`.
- The `theme-color` schematic in this repo bundles material-color-utilities and therefore generates tone 80, so its output disagrees with the system tokens in the same package.

Tone 90 came in with #29655, which followed #29577. That issue relied on Theme Builder screenshots, and the Theme Builder labeled the dark `On Surface Var.` swatch "NV-90". That label was wrong: the swatch itself is tone 80, as already reported in material-foundation/material-theme-builder#301 (May 2024). The pixels in the screenshot attached to #29577 confirm this. The same PR changed `surface-container-highest` because of a mislabeled swatch, and #29902 reverted that change.

Because the tones are equal, `on-surface` and `on-surface-variant` render identically in the dark scheme whenever the neutral and neutral-variant palettes are close or equal. As a result, form field placeholders look like entered values, and labels and hint texts lose their visual hierarchy.

### Reproduction

No StackBlitz reproduction: the wrong value is a static token mapping and can be read directly in [`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24).

To see the effect:

1. Generate a theme with `ng generate @angular/material:theme-color` and the same color for neutral and neutral-variant, e.g. `#ececed`.
2. Render a `mat-form-field` with `appearance="outline"`, a placeholder and `floatLabel="always"`, next to a filled one, in the dark scheme.

### Expected Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to `neutral-variant` tone 80 in the dark scheme. Placeholders are visibly dimmer than entered values.

### Actual Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to tone 90, the same tone as `--mat-sys-on-surface`. Placeholders and values are indistinguishable.

### Environment

- Angular Material: 22.2.6
- Still present on `main` (fcec64761)

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/scrolling): prevent nested tables from inheriting outer viewport
Issues.Body:
Hi! This fixes ordinary tables inside `*cdkVirtualFor` items throwing `CdkVirtualScrollViewport is already attached.` on initial render.

Fixes #34121.

### What changes

An inner table can resolve the outer `CDK_VIRTUAL_SCROLL_VIEWPORT` token and enable table virtualization, even though `cdkVirtualFor` already owns that viewport.

Provide `null` for this token on `CdkVirtualForOf`, alongside the existing `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` boundary introduced in #34100. This lets tables inside the repeated items render normally. The repeater itself resolves its owning viewport using `skipSelf`, and an independent nested viewport provides its own token.

This also means custom consumers of `CDK_VIRTUAL_SCROLL_VIEWPORT` inside virtual-for items resolve `null` instead of implicitly inheriting the outer viewport.

### Regression coverage

Add a test with ordinary tables inside virtual-for items. It checks that each table renders all of its rows without virtual-table fixed layout, both initially and after scrolling. It also checks that the outer viewport retains the correct data length and advances its rendered range.

Before the fix, the new test fails with the reported error; the other 89 CDK table tests pass.

### Validation

Completed locally:

- CDK table: Chromium (90 passed) and Firefox (90 passed).
- CDK scrolling: Chromium (109 passed).
- Material table: Chromium (36 passed).
- Repository formatter, targeted TSLint, and `git diff --check`.

The standalone reproduction linked in #34121 was also verified in Chrome using published Angular/CDK 22.2.6.

Issues.Title: bug(cdk/table): ordinary tables inside cdkVirtualFor throw "viewport is already attached"
Issues.Body:
Hi! An ordinary `cdk-table` inside a `*cdkVirtualFor` item throws `CdkVirtualScrollViewport is already attached.` on initial render. ### Is this a regression? I haven't verified the last working version. ### Description I want to virtualize a list of groups, with a small, ordinary table inside each group. Only the outer list should use virtual scrolling; each table should display all of its own rows. When the viewport and the item template are declared in the same component, the inner table picks up the outer viewport and tries to attach to it, even though `cdkVirtualFor` is already using it. ### Reproduction [Open the reproduction in StackBlitz](https://stackblitz.com/github/nagahara-naoki/components/tree/repro-nested-table-virtual-scroll) [Source code and local run instructions](https://github.com/nagahara-naoki/components/tree/repro-nested-table-virtual-scroll) 1. Open the reproduction and wait for the app to start. 2. Open the browser console. 3. The error appears on initial render. No scrolling or other interaction is needed. The relevant template is: ```html
{{row}}
``` The component imports `ScrollingModule` and `CdkTableModule`, and uses this data: ```ts groups = Array.from({length: 100}, (_, id) => ({ rows: Array.from({length: 3}, (_, row) => `Group ${id}, row ${row}`), })); ``` To run locally: `npm ci`, then `npm start`. ### Expected Behavior The viewport scrolls through the groups, and each group's table renders its three rows normally. ### Actual Behavior Initial rendering throws: ```text Error: CdkVirtualScrollViewport is already attached. at CdkVirtualScrollViewport.attach at CdkTable._setupVirtualScrolling at CdkTable.ngAfterContentInit ``` ### Environment - Angular: 22.2.6 - CDK: 22.2.6 - Browser: Chrome 157.0.8103.51 - Operating system: macOS I also reproduced this in a Chromium regression test against repository commit `32cf96285e1b0ae4183f0f6f1992bbe62ace4426`. ### Additional context This looks related to the dependency injection boundary addressed in #34100. That change prevents `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` from leaking into virtual-for items. In this case, the inner table still resolves the outer `CDK_VIRTUAL_SCROLL_VIEWPORT` token.

Issues.Title: fix(material/sort): use initial start direction for unsorted header arrows
Issues.Body:
Bind `.mat-sort-header-descending` and `.mat-sort-header-ascending` on the sort header container via `_getArrowDirection()` so that:
- When a header is actively sorted (`_isSorted()`), it displays the active `_sort.direction`.
- When a header is unsorted (`!_isSorted()`), its hover/focus hint arrow reflects its own initial sort direction (`this.start || this._sort.start`) instead of inheriting another sorted column's `_sort.direction`.

### Verification
- Strict Angular template/TypeScript type-check (`ngc`) and `tslint` on `src/material/sort`
- Prettier formatting check on modified files
- Executed all 27 unit specs in `src/material/sort/sort.spec.ts` (including the new regression test verifying unsorted headers retain their initial `start` direction while another header is sorted `'desc'` and when `matSortStart` changes) in headless Chrome with `TestBed` and `Jasmine` (27 passed, 0 failed)

Fixes #33933

Issues.Title: feat(material/select): add a styling token for the panel shape
Issues.Body:
Adds a `container-shape` token to `select-overrides` so the border radius of the select panel can
be customized. Previously it was hardcoded to 4px, while the autocomplete and menu panels already
expose the same token.

The default rendering doesn't change. In M3 the value comes from `corner-extra-small`, so apps that
customize that system token will see the select panel follow it, like the autocomplete and menu
panels.

Apps can set it with `mat.select-overrides((container-shape: ...))`.
